1.mascotDialogue: Same values, two views — a tree for the ordering rule, an array for how it truly lives in memory. parent(i) equals (i minus 1) divided by 2. This is the entire address book.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3 is the bridge between array and tree — any index's parent is always (i-1)/2, integer division, no rounding. Line 4 is the min-heap rule itself — stop the moment the parent is already smaller or equal.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover index 4 in the array — watch its tree node answer, as a child of index 1. Same data, two windows, moving together.

4.mascotDialogue: Both the array cell and the tree node glow the same broken color at once — because it is one mistake, only seen from two angles.
